decisions.summary: A .drawing.html listed under Entry: is refused at parse, the message naming Drawing:
decisions.why: Enforcement test: a guard that REFUSES, so its reach was measured. _base.py:331 sits inside _about_feature, so it refuses only an About-form modal (the 149 old-form files still listing drawing pages under Entry: today parse untouched), and only on the '.drawing.html' substring of Entry:, which is exactly the set of 'how our maps draw it' pages. Entry: is what sources.research_questions puts on the References tab, so the refusal enforces FR-006 and SC-008 ('no References tab lists a how our maps draw it page') and nothing else; delete that requirement and the refusal has nothing to check. Refusing at import is the established form for every other About-form error (Label:, old prose tags). No reach beyond the request.

decisions.why: FR-014's check, its three criteria one for one ('every convention and standardization ... told with its real counterpart, nothing is claimed that is not drawn, and its links are exactly the drawing pages'); the GM asked for 'a specification for the subagent check'. Tier is a design matter; FR-014 asks only that it be pinned.

decisions.summary: The modal-depiction bundle carries a screenshot crop of the glyph on a pool page (fixed zoom, the page tests' browser); a kind on no pool map bundled without one, saying so
decisions.why: Enforcement test: an INPUT to the requested check, not new behavior - it refuses, blocks and rewrites nothing. FR-014 asks the check to judge the tab 'as drawn' and that 'nothing is claimed that is not drawn'; the drawing pages say what the rules are, the crop is the only thing in the bundle that shows what the glyph actually looks like. Delete the Depiction check and the crop has nothing to serve. The session pitched 'a crop of the glyph' to the GM before his 2026-10-04 reply, which raised no objection. The no-crop fallback does not skip the check (pages and claims rows still go in).

decisions.summary: The bundle carries the claims-index rows whose cited pages include the kind's drawing pages

Does it do what it says: measured in dev/claims-index.json, the farmhouse's DRIFTED rows (HousesMixin.house#farmhouse glyph, #ridge at 0.6 of the length - the roof shape knob, #big farmhouse wing) all cite 0029-farmhouses-minka.drawing.html, so the filter reaches the single-roof drift the plan names.

decisions.summary: LINKS judged against 'the drawing pages the modal and its KIND rest on'; the bundle carries CANDIDATE drawing pages beyond Drawing: - (a) the sibling of each Entry question and (b) any drawing page the modal listed at the merge base (scripts/_modal_bundle.py drawing_candidates)
decisions.why: Round 3's required change, applied and confirmed in round 4. scripts/_modal_owed.py modals_at gains about_only (default True) and passes it to modals_in; scripts/_modal_bundle.py drawing_candidates now reads the base with modals_at(root, base, about_only=False), so an old-form docstring at the merge base is read and every .drawing.html under its Entry: (or Drawing:) becomes a candidate - leg (b) is live for the conversion case FR-012 makes universal. Both legs now reach what the decision states: (a) the sibling drawing page of each Entry question, (b) any drawing page the base listed in either form. test_a_drawing_page_the_old_form_listed_at_the_base_is_a_candidate_after_the_conversion isolates leg (b): the base is an old-form Farmhouse listing 0038-yards.drawing.html, the head cites only 0029 (whose drawing page does not exist in the fixture tree) with no Drawing:, so the candidate can come from the base read alone, and with about_only=True it would be skipped. Re-run in round 4: make test-file green, 10,989 passed. LINKS is judged against the drawing pages the modal and its KIND rest on (FR-014, SC-008, the GM: 'in cases where no such sections exist we would omit the tab'). No narrowing remains.
